leaves.what: The four cards' grid (a ul, two columns on a phone, four on a desktop) and each card's insides: name, figure, and a change line with a lucide trend icon and the words Up/Down.
leaves.why: Expected: the kit has no figure or stat card; CardContent is headline, supporting text and actions.

leaves.what: Wrote <Label component="h3">, <Label component="p"> (twice) and <Headline component="p">: four type errors. Second attempt: Title size small as the h3, div for the others.
leaves.why: Each type primitive takes its own short list of elements (Label: div, label, span; Headline: div, h1-h6, span). The lists are in the types only; the doc comment at the top of Typography.tsx does not give them.

leaves.what: Read Typography.tsx's types after the errors, for the elements each primitive takes and for colorRole.
leaves.why: The element lists are not in the doc comment.

parts.notes: The change line's colour is primary for good news and error for bad; the words and the arrow carry the meaning. Not seen in a browser: the truncation of a long figure at phone width is unverified. The change line may wrap to two lines at phone width while its placeholder is one, so a card's height may move a line when it arrives: unverified.

leaves.what: The card's column: one progress indicator (a month-end invoice run that advances on a timer) and four meters (revenue against the range's goal, trials converted, seats, emails over the plan).
leaves.why: Expected.

parts.notes: The revenue goal is a Meter, not a ProgressIndicator: a reading for a range, by the kit's own distinction. The meter over its range says so in its label, as Meter's comment asks. Both served as documented. The loaded state was rendered to a string once (4 meters, 1 progressbar, their value texts right); not seen in a browser.

leaves.what: Used DateRangePicker as it is: its calendar opens full screen at every width.
leaves.why: There is no docked or popover range picker. For a filter on a desktop dashboard a full-screen dialog is heavy; a range calendar in a popover would serve better. Typing in the field stays quick.

leaves.what: Read DatePicker.tsx's prop types (FieldProps, DateRangePickerProps) for supportingText, className and what the range picker refuses.
leaves.why: The doc comment names the layouts and the draft; the field's own props are only in the types.

leaves.what: The filter row that holds the period toggle and the field, stacked on a phone.
leaves.why: Expected.

parts.notes: Two states are kept, the field's value (may be null, half-typed or refused) and the applied range, so only a whole range that ends by today reaches the figures. A range that ends after today is refused by maxValue and not applied. Unverified in a browser: the field's width at 400px with two dates and the calendar button.

leaves.what: Controlled the selection and ignored the empty set in onSelectionChange, instead of disallowEmptySelection.
leaves.why: The toggle must show nothing selected when the range typed in the field is no period, yet a press on the selected period must not unselect it. The group has one switch for both.

leaves.what: Read ButtonGroup.tsx past its comment for the selection props it forwards (selectedKeys, onSelectionChange) and Button.tsx's toggle types.
leaves.why: The comment says the children are Buttons with isToggle and an id, with no example of a connected, selected group.

leaves.what: A visible Label above the group, tied with aria-labelledby, and the row that holds the toggle and the date field.
leaves.why: Expected.

parts.notes: Week, Month and Quarter write the last 7, 30 or 90 days into the date range; a range typed by hand that is none of them leaves the toggle empty. Chose ButtonGroup connected over SegmentedButton because the kit's comment says to.

leaves.what: The placeholder area: a dashed outline-variant frame, an icon, the words "Chart slot" and what the chart library draws there.
leaves.why: Expected: a slot is the project's.

parts.notes: No chart is drawn, as the screen asks.

leaves.what: Put ListItem in a plain ul/li and overrode its cursor with className="cursor-default".
leaves.why: The rows are read, not pressed, so GridList's focus and keyboard would promise an action there is none of. ListItem draws cursor-pointer always and has no read-only form.

leaves.what: Wrapped Avatar in an aria-hidden span.
leaves.why: Without src and alt, Avatar is role="img" with no name; with alt it repeats the name the headline already says. It has no decorative form.

leaves.what: Read ListItem.tsx's styles (the cursor, the state layer's group classes) and Avatar.tsx's markup (the role).
leaves.why: Neither is in the doc comment. ListItem's example also writes <Avatar name="Ada" />, a prop Avatar does not have.

leaves.what: The card's heading, the count line, and "Show 6 more" under the list.
leaves.why: Expected.

leaves.what: "Show 6 more" paging by hand: a text Button under the list that reveals six more rows; on its last press the list (tabIndex -1) takes the focus the button held.
leaves.why: pager-block may have served here, but `npx shadcn@latest add @ds/pager-block -y` was refused by this session's permission system, so the block was never seen. Not worked around.

leaves.what: Read EmptyState.tsx's props and markup for its sizes and the bare form.
leaves.why: Its comment gives the bare className; the `size` values are in the styles.

parts.notes: The list follows the date range, shows six rows and six more on each press; an empty range would show EmptyState (the mock data has an event every day, so it is not reached). A quarter holds about 170 events, six at a time: a pager would serve that better than "Show more"; see the leave on the block. The focus move on the last press is reasoned, not tried in a browser.

parts.part: A state for each card while it loads

leaves.what: A Placeholder (a pulsing surface-container-highest bar) written by hand, laid out as each card's content: figure and change, five bars, six rows. The chart slot shows LoadingIndicator.
leaves.why: The kit has no skeleton or placeholder component; LoadingIndicator in seven cards at once would be seven spinners.

leaves.what: animate-pulse (Tailwind's own keyframes and timing), stopped under reduced motion.
leaves.why: The kit's motion tokens are durations and easings; there is no looping animation to name.

leaves.what: VisuallyHidden from react-aria-components, for the hidden "Loading" text, the page's polite status and a hidden heading.
leaves.why: ds-build lists it as coming straight from React Aria and not a leave; logged because the brief's `hook` kind covers a utility.

parts.notes: A useLoading hook gives each card its own wait (0.5s to 1.9s) after the range, the period or Refresh changes, with aria-busy on the card. Only the loading branch runs before effects, so both branches were rendered to a string once to check them; the pulse and the timing were not seen in a browser.

general_leaves.what: The page: a main on surface, a header with the title and a Refresh IconButton, the filters, the cards' grids.
Read IconButton.tsx's prop types for `icon`, `variant` and the required aria-label.
No block is used. Whether one serves was not established: the one `shadcn add` tried (pager-block) was refused by the session's permission system, so none of the five was read.
general_leaves.why: The blocks are not in the project until added, and nothing in the installed files shows what a block contains.

general_leaves.what: Boundary slip: a throwaway check script was first written to a folder beside the project (scratchpad/_tmp_04) and removed at once; the check was then run from src/ and deleted.

friction: Nothing was seen in a browser, so the layout at 400px and in dark is reasoned, not checked. Hard to find: (1) which elements each type primitive accepts as `component` (four type errors): one line a primitive in its doc comment would do. (2) What a loading card should be: the kit has LoadingIndicator and ProgressIndicator and says nothing about placeholders; a Skeleton, or a sentence in ds-build saying it is the project's, would settle it. (3) A list that is only read: ListItem's comment says GridListItem gives it its behaviour, and nothing says what to do when there is none; its example passes Avatar a `name` prop that does not exist. (4) A selected connected ButtonGroup: an example with selectionMode, selectedKeys and Button isToggle id in the comment would have saved reading the source. (5) DateRangePicker is full screen only, which the comment says plainly; a docked range picker is what a filter wants.
